name: RET / RET-CR / RET-N
aliases: Radar Echo Telescope for Cosmic Rays
summary: A radar-detection programme uses an implemented cosmic-ray pathfinder in Greenland to develop technology for a future neutrino observatory. RET-CR tests cascades entering ice; RET-N is the proposed neutrino array.
detection_principle: An energetic particle cascade ionises ice, temporarily creating a radio-reflecting plasma. A transmitter illuminates the ice and receivers search for a radar echo; cosmic-ray triggers and accelerator tests validate the method before neutrino observations.

sites.name: RET-CR site near Summit Station, Greenland
sites.location: RET-CR site near Summit Station, Greenland

status.label: Multiple stages
status.evidence: RET-CR is an implemented cosmic-ray pathfinder with 2023 and 2024 field data. RET-N remains a proposed neutrino array in the 2026 contribution.

timeline.event: T576 accelerator measurements demonstrated radar echoes from particle cascades.
Improved RET-CR field campaign collected further data.
RET-N remained a future neutrino-observatory concept in conference studies.

collaboration.name: RET / RET-CR / RET-N Collaboration
collaboration.participants_note: Institutions listed here are selected participants named in the cited project publications.

key_parameters.name: First field exposure
key_parameters.value: May 2023 deployment, four-week commissioning, then nine days of data

phases.name: T576 accelerator validation
phases.description: Electron-beam-induced cascades provided a controlled demonstration of radar echoes, distinct from neutrino observation.

phases.name: RET-CR Greenland pathfinder
phases.description: Cosmic-ray-triggered field instrument with 2023 and 2024 campaigns.

phases.name: RET-N neutrino observatory
phases.description: A future in-ice neutrino detector developed from pathfinder measurements. Its full-scale site and configuration are not fixed by these sources.

results.summary: RET-CR initial performance demonstrated technical operation of a radar-based particle-cascade detector in ice. This did not establish detection of astrophysical neutrinos.

science_scope: Published limits are not neutrino detections. Instrument or exposure parameters refer to the explicitly named campaign; research prototypes and future designs are distinguished.
